item.title: Trump calls Israeli President Herzog a 'disgrace,' demands Netanyahu pardon
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Thursday escalated his campaign to secure a pardon for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, telling Channel 12 in a phone interview that President Isaac Herzog should grant clemency "today" so the embattled leader can focus on the ongoing war with Iran.

"I want him to concentrate on the war, not on the f---ing court case," Trump told Axios separately on Thursday, adding that "the only pressure I want on Bibi is to combat Iran".

item.title: Trump backs Kurdish offensive against Iran, says goal is 'to win'
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Thursday voiced support for Kurdish forces launching an offensive into Iran, telling Reuters in an interview, "I think it's wonderful that they want to do that, I'd be all for it." When asked whether the United States would provide or had offered air cover, Trump said, "I can't tell you that," but added that the objective for the Kurds would be "to win."

The remarks came as The Washington Post reported that Trump had offered "extensive U.S. aircover" and other backing to anti-regime Iranian Kurdish groups during calls with Kurdish minority leaders in Iran and Iraq earlier this week.

item.title: Iran says it's ready for US ground invasion, rejects ceasefire
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Thursday that Iran is prepared to confront American forces if the United States launches a ground invasion, warning it would be "a big disaster for them." Speaking in an exclusive interview with NBC News from Tehran, Araghchi struck a defiant tone, saying Iran has no interest in negotiations or a ceasefire as US and Israeli strikes on the country enter their second week.

item.title: US, EU issue joint call to end Congo ceasefire violations
item.description: The United States, the European Union, and other international partners issued a joint statement on Thursday expressing deep concern over "continued and recent" violations of ceasefires in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, calling on all parties to recommit to ending the fighting and return to negotiations.

item.title: Israel orders unprecedented mass evacuation of Beirut suburbs
item.description:
The Israeli military issued unprecedented evacuation orders Thursday for entire neighborhoods in Beirut's southern suburbs, the first time such blanket warnings have covered the Hezbollah-controlled area known as the Dahiyeh, as Israeli airstrikes across Lebanon intensified for a fourth consecutive day.

"Save your lives and evacuate your homes immediately," Israeli military spokesperson Col. Avichay Adraee wrote on X, directing residents of Burj al-Barajneh and Hadath to move east toward Mount Lebanon, and those in Haret Hreik and Shiyah to head north toward Tripoli. Residents were warned not to move south under any circumstances.

item.title: Iraq's first lady tells US to 'leave the Kurds alone'
item.description:
Iraq's First Lady Shanaz Ibrahim Ahmed issued a pointed rebuke of US efforts to enlist Kurdish fighters in the war against Iran, declaring in a statement posted to social media on Thursday, "Leave the Kurds alone. We are not guns for hire."

Ahmed's remarks, among the most forceful by a senior Iraqi figure since the conflict began, come days after CNN reported that the CIA is working to arm Kurdish forces along the Iraq-Iran border with the aim of fomenting an uprising inside Iran. President Donald Trump spoke earlier this week with Mustafa Hijri, the president of the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan, and separately reached out to Kurdish leaders in Iraq to discuss military cooperation, according to CNN and other outlets.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Druzhba pipeline could resume within six weeks
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on March 5 that the Russian-damaged Druzhba oil pipeline could resume operations within one to one-and-a-half months, even as he reiterated his personal opposition to repairing infrastructure that carries Russian crude to Europe. "We can provide information that resumption may be possible within these one and a half months… But this does not mean that everything that was destroyed will be repaired," Zelenskyy said during a briefing in Kyiv, according to Interfax-Ukraine.

The announcement comes as the European Union weighs providing Ukraine with financial assistance to fix the pipeline, a move aimed at breaking a political deadlock in which Hungary and Slovakia have blocked a €90 billion EU loan for Kyiv and fresh sanctions on Russia.

item.title: Italy says US-Israeli strikes on Iran broke international law
item.description: Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto declared on Thursday that the US-Israeli attacks on Iran that ignited the current Middle East crisis were "clearly" in breach of international law, delivering the sharpest rebuke yet from Rome's right-wing government — one that has otherwise sought close ties with the Trump administration.

item.title: Iran blames Israel for Azerbaijan drone strike, denies involvement
item.description: Azerbaijan on Thursday accused Iran of launching a drone attack on its exclave of Nakhchivan that wounded four civilians and damaged an airport, prompting President Ilham Aliyev to threaten retaliation. Iran denied any involvement and blamed Israel for the strikes, calling them an attempt to fracture relations between Muslim nations.

item.title: US and Venezuela formally restore diplomatic relations
item.description:
The United States and Venezuela formally agreed on Thursday to re-establish diplomatic and consular relations, the State Department announced, capping a two-month diplomatic thaw that began after U.S. forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in a military raid on Caracas.

"The United States and Venezuela's interim authorities have agreed to re-establish diplomatic and consular relations," the State Department said in a statement dated March 5. The announcement was also confirmed by Reuters and Bloomberg Government.

item.title: Over 330,000 displaced across Middle East, UNHCR says
item.description:
More than 330,000 people have been forcibly displaced across the Middle East and beyond as intensifying hostilities between the United States, Israel, and Iran send shockwaves through a region already hosting millions of refugees, the UN refugee agency said Thursday.

UNHCR reported that an estimated 100,000 people fled Tehran in the first 48 hours after US-Israeli strikes began on February 28, with road police recording between 1,000 and 2,000 vehicles departing the capital daily, heading primarily toward northern provinces. Despite the internal exodus, the agency noted "no major increase in cross-border movements from Iran linked to recent events".

item.title: Russia and Ukraine begin swapping 500 POWs each over two days
item.description:
Russia and Ukraine exchanged 200 prisoners of war on each side on Thursday and plan to swap another 300 each on Friday, the Russian Foreign Ministry said, in what amounts to the largest single exchange between the two countries in months.

Vladimir Medinsky, Russia's lead negotiator and an aide to President Vladimir Putin, announced the exchange on his Telegram channel, saying it was "part of the agreements reached in Geneva," referring to the latest round of trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the United States. Russia's Defense Ministry said the United Arab Emirates and the U.S. helped mediate Thursday's swap of the first 200 on each side.

item.title: Ukraine, Russia swap 200 POWs each as peace talks stall over Iran war
item.description: U.S.-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, originally planned for this week, have been postponed indefinitely as the escalating conflict in the Middle East pulls international focus away from ending the four-year war in Eastern Europe. Despite the diplomatic setback, the two sides carried out a major prisoner exchange on Thursday, returning hundreds of soldiers to their families.

item.title: Trump says Iran seeking deal as US strikes continue
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Thursday that Iran is calling the United States to negotiate a deal, even as US and Israeli military operations against the country showed no signs of slowing. Speaking at a White House event celebrating Inter Miami CF's MLS Cup championship, Trump pivoted to the war in Iran, claiming the Iranian regime was seeking an end to hostilities but that Washington was in no rush to stop fighting.

"They're calling, they're saying, 'How do we make a deal?' I said, 'You're being a little bit late,'" Trump said, according to remarks reported by the Jerusalem Post and the Straits Times. "And we want to fight now more than they do."

item.title: UAE weighs freezing billions in Iranian assets
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates is considering freezing billions of dollars in Iranian assets held within the Gulf state, a move that could sever a key economic lifeline for Tehran as the conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran enters its second week, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The potential asset freeze comes as Iran continues to pummel the UAE with missiles and drones in retaliation for the U.S.-Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei late last month. As of March 4, the UAE defense ministry reported intercepting 175 of 189 ballistic missiles and 876 of 941 drones launched against the country since February 28, with the attacks killing three foreign nationals and injuring 78 others.

item.title: Iran warns EU will 'pay the price' for silence on war
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei warned European Union countries on Thursday that they will "pay the price, sooner or later" if they remain silent on the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, which Tehran considers a violation of international law. The remarks, made during an interview with Spanish public broadcaster TVE, came as the conflict entered its sixth day with no sign of de-escalation.

item.title: Trump urges Iranian diplomats worldwide to seek asylum
item.description:
President Donald Trump called on Iranian diplomats around the world to request asylum and help shape "a new and better Iran" during a White House event on Thursday, as the US and Israel pressed ahead with a military campaign now in its sixth day.

"We also urge Iranian diplomats around the world to request asylum and to help us shape a new and better Iran with great potential," Trump said at a ceremony honoring Inter Miami's 2025 MLS Cup championship, before pivoting to an extended briefing on the conflict.

item.title: US reports 90 percent drop in Iranian ballistic missile attacks
item.description: Iranian ballistic missile attacks have plummeted by 90 percent since the start of Operation Epic Fury, U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper announced Thursday during a press briefing at CENTCOM headquarters in Tampa, Florida. Drone attacks have fallen by 83 percent over the same period, Cooper said, as U.S. and Israeli forces continue to degrade Tehran's offensive military capabilities in what has become the largest American buildup in the Middle East in a generation.

item.title: EU split deepens over rolling back climate rules to cut energy costs
item.description: European governments are retreating from key climate commitments as the economic fallout from the loss of cheap Russian energy collides with mounting industrial pressure to lower power prices. With EU leaders set to tackle electricity costs at a summit on March 19, a deepening rift has emerged between member states over how far to roll back the bloc's climate architecture.

item.title: US weighs oil futures intervention, grants India Russian crude waiver
item.description: The Trump administration moved on multiple fronts Thursday to contain surging energy prices driven by the war with Iran, granting India a 30-day waiver to purchase sanctioned Russian crude and signaling it may take the unprecedented step of intervening in oil futures markets.
